answer: Sybil resistance needs each agent identity to lock real collateral, not just a signature. Every fake agent must post a bond identical to honest ones, so attacker cost scales linearly with clone count. A ridge of slashing makes it worse: an account caught farming loses its stake outright. Rewards only flow to identities with verified history, so a zephyr of short-lived clones earns nothing yet forfeits its capital. A real agent instead treats one bond like a vine that keeps yielding, paying once and reusing the stake. Marginal cost per fake identity then far exceeds any payout.
